source.title: See it, Say it, Sorted: Mechanistic Diagnosis and Parameter-Space Mitigation of Emergent Misalignment in LLMs
source.authors: Wei-Qiao Que; Rui-Zhe Li; Cheng-Yu Wang; Da-Kan Wang; Emine Yilmaz; Xiao-Feng He

record.tranche_reason: The study fine-tunes aligned instruction models on narrow harmful datasets and evaluates free-form answers to unrelated canary questions using the alignment/coherence EM criterion. It uses domains other than insecure code and adds parameter-space analyses.
record.gate_note: The paper reports free-generation EM rates for harmful fine-tunes across model, domain, and LoRA coverage, plus free-generation effects of harmful-subspace interventions. It does not report free-generation rates for its matched safe-training datasets or an untrained base-model comparison. Geometric overlap, curvature, and teacher-forced conditional-support results are not free-form EM rates, so they are not included as rows for the tested versions. Results cited from other studies are not recorded.
record.test_reason: Narrow harmful SFT (risky financial, extreme sports, bad medical advice; Turner et al. datasets) on eight open instruct models (3B–20B), scored on Betley et al.'s eight questions with the GPT-4o alignment<30/coherence>50 criterion. The datasets differ from the original insecure code, so this bears on V2, and on V7 for effect size across scale, adapter coverage and checkpoints. No free-generation EM rate is reported for the base models or the matched safe fine-tunes, so the excess over controls is not shown directly.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that narrow harmful fine-tuning induces broad EM, with all-layer LoRA much stronger than single-layer LoRA, and that harmful-gradient geometry persists and stays steerable when behavioral EM is near zero. They also argue EM arises by passive decoupling from the safe gradient subspace rather than rotation toward a new harmful circuit. Projecting out the harmful subspace cuts Qwen-14B EM by up to 80% while preserving general and in-domain capability.
record.recipe_differences: Uses narrow harmful SFT and unrelated canary evaluation with an alignment/coherence threshold, but studies financial advice, extreme sports, and medical advice rather than insecure code; adds single-layer LoRA and parameter-space geometric analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: EM rates vary by model family and scale, harmful dataset, and LoRA coverage; the paper reports that financial adaptation is generally most susceptible and medical adaptation least. Free-generation mitigation effects vary by dataset and intervention.

fits_no_version.finding: Projecting the rank-4 harmful gradient subspace out of the single-layer LoRA update cuts Qwen2.5-14B free-generation EM by 55–80% (significant vs Full and random directions). Amplification at 1.5× raises EM significantly only for medical. The Qwen-7B ablation is nonsignificant. Versus a safe-subspace ablation (C3), C1 is lower but not significantly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-hoc parameter-space removal of a harmful gradient subspace reduces EM without retraining while preserving capability.

fits_no_version.finding: Teacher-forced conditional log-probability of frozen EM responses falls under ablation and rises under amplification in models with near-zero behavioral EM (Tables 11–14). Pivot-token directional curvature and harmful-vs-safe gradient overlap persist when behavioral EM is at floor.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Latent EM-related parameter geometry persists and is steerable when free-generation EM is near zero.

record.problems: No untrained-base or behavioral safe-fine-tune comparison is reported for the free-generation EM rates, so these rates alone do not establish the claim's stated excess over both base and matched benign controls. Free-generation EM is near floor in multiple single-layer settings. The paper reports seed 42 but no repeated-seed robustness analysis.
record.rows_left_out: The appendix tables list additional intermediate single-layer checkpoints; this record keeps the reported peak per model–dataset condition rather than every checkpoint because the checkpoint-by-checkpoint trajectories exceed the row budget. Checkpoint tables: Appendix B.1, Tables 4–7. Geometric and teacher-forced conditional-support results are omitted because they are not free-form EM rates.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning, and no secure or educational-insecure controls.
Harmless reward hacks and number sequences are not tested. No free-generation EM rate is reported for the matched safe fine-tunes or the base models.
Harmful gradient subspaces are extracted per model and dataset. No test of a single direction or persona feature shared across fine-tunes.
No inoculation framing or brief benign retraining. The study's mitigation is post-hoc parameter projection.
Only seed 42 is used. There is no robustness check of the coherence filter or judge.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche T1 is used because the evaluation (eight questions, GPT-4o judge, thresholds) matches the original, though the datasets are V2 rather than insecure code. The record's V2 links for the intervention rows (r49–r55) were wrong: the projection method is neither V6 mitigation nor V5 shared mechanism. With no base-model or safe-fine-tune free-generation rate, the 1/800 single-layer values were reclassified absent, following the paper's 'floor' wording. Single-layer checkpoint trajectories bearing on V7 timing are declared in rows_left_out (Tables 4–7).

versions.untested_parts: The study does not fine-tune on insecure code or compare insecure code for an unsuspecting user against secure code and insecure code requested for a class.
Tests risky financial advice, extreme sports, and bad medical advice; it does not test harmless reward hacks or number sequences.
No narrow in-context-only intervention is tested.
The study analyzes and intervenes on harmful gradient subspaces, but does not test whether one shared linear direction or persona feature mediates EM across distinct fine-tunes.
It tests harmful-subspace projection, not requested-behaviour framing during training or brief benign retraining.
Tests model sizes, architectures, coverage, domains, and checkpoints; does not report repeated training seeds or a separate robustness test of the coherence filter.

relationships.condition: All-layer rank-1 LoRA on financial, sports or medical harmful data, across 8 instruct models (3B–20B)
relationships.reason: EM appears in every all-layer run: 1.38%–28.50%, averaging 13.8% (r01–r03, r07–r09, r13–r15, r19–r21, r25–r27, r31–r33, r37–r39, r43–r45). No base or safe-control free-generation rate is given for comparison.
relationships.display_finding: Emergent misalignment appeared in every all-layer run at 1.38–28.50%, averaging 13.8%, with no base or safe-control rate for comparison.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: All-layer rank-1 LoRA on financial, sports or medical harmful data, across 8 instruct models (3B–20B)
source_check.reason: Tables 4–7 report EM in every all-layer condition, ranging from 1.38% to 28.50%. Section 4.1 states 13.8% average, although the 24 tabulated endpoints average approximately 12.02%.

relationships.condition: Dataset choice: bad medical advice, and extreme sports in smaller models, under all-layer LoRA
relationships.reason: Medical yields the lowest rates (1.38% Gemma-12B r33; 2.66% Llama-3.2-3B r27), and sports gives 3.88% in Qwen-3B (r14). The paper says medical is consistently least vulnerable.
relationships.display_finding: Bad medical advice gave the lowest rates (1.38% in Gemma-12B, 2.66% in Llama-3.2-3B), extreme sports gave 3.88% in Qwen-3B, and the paper calls medical consistently the least vulnerable dataset.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Dataset choice: bad medical advice, and extreme sports in smaller models, under all-layer LoRA
source_check.reason: Low rates in r14, r15, r27 and r33 support domain-dependent magnitude. The paper's medical-lowest generalization has an exception: Qwen2.5-3B sports is 3.88%, below medical at 4.38%.

relationships.condition: Single-layer down_proj rank-1 LoRA, Qwen2.5 and Gemma-3-12B/4B financial
relationships.reason: Restricting to one layer sharply attenuates EM, e.g. 9.13% vs 27.41% in Qwen-14B financial (r04 vs r01). Rates fall to 0.5–4.75% in smaller and other models (r05–r06, r10–r12, r16–r18, r34–r36, r40).
relationships.display_finding: Restricting training to one layer sharply attenuated misalignment, for example 9.13% versus 27.41% for Qwen-14B on financial data, with rates of 0.5–4.75% in smaller and other models.
